Base.description: Base is a base-image repository and its newest observed version.

consumers.description: Consumers is how many images are built on it; StaleConsumers how many of those aren't on the newest version.

versions.description: Versions is how many versions of it images are built on.

BaseLink.description: BaseLink is an image's base and how current it is.

currentRef.description: CurrentRef and CurrentDigest are the newest observed version of the base.

drift.description: Drift is current, stale, or unknown.

imageId.description: ImageID is the base's ID when the base is itself in the report.

method.description: Method is how the relationship was established: layer-prefix (the image starts with the base's exact layers), oci-base-digest, buildpacks-metadata, oci-base-name, or history.

ref.description: Ref is the base as the image is built on it (repository:tag or repository@digest).

strength.description: Strength is proof (layer-prefix), declared (an exact claim by the image's author), assisted (a partial claim), or weak.

BaseSummary.description: BaseSummary counts images by how their base is known and how current it is.

claimed.description: Claimed bases rest on something the image's author wrote (labels, annotations, build history).

proven.description: Proven bases were established by layer digests.

roots.description: Roots have no parent: base images, or images built from scratch or by composing layers (Nix, apko).

unresolved.description: Unresolved images have no base that could be determined (see each image's unresolved reasons).

Builder.description: Builder is how the image was built, as far as its metadata tells.

basis.description: Basis says what the classification rests on.

kind.description: Kind names the builder: clearcutt-factory, buildkit, docker, buildpacks, nix, apko, debuerreotype, or unknown. Open: new builders may appear, so show unknown values as they are.

Evidence.description: Evidence is what is known about each kind of supply-chain evidence.

rebase.description: Rebase is a clearcutt-factory rebase record, for images whose layers were moved onto a newer base without a rebuild.

recipe.description: Recipe is a clearcutt-factory recipe: what anyone needs to rebuild the image bit for bit.

sbom.description: SBOM is a software bill of materials (CycloneDX or SPDX).

signature.description: Signature is a signature over the image itself.

tests.description: Tests is evidence that the image was tested (a smoke test or test attestation).

vulnerabilityScan.description: VulnerabilityScan is a vulnerability report about the image.

EvidenceItem.description: EvidenceItem is one kind of evidence for one image.

detail.description: Detail explains the status in a sentence.

platforms.description: Platforms gives the status per platform image, for evidence attached per platform (SBOMs and vulnerability reports); Status is the worst.

predicateType.description: PredicateType is the in-toto predicate type, for attestations.

ref.description: Ref is where it is stored (e.g. an attestation's repository@digest).

signer.description: Signer is who signed it, as read from the signing certificate or key.

source.description: Source is where it was found: cosign-signature, cosign-attestation, github-attestation, or oci-referrer (an unsigned document). Open: new sources may appear.

status.description: Status is verified (found and checked against a trusted signer), present (found but not checked: no trusted signer applies, or it can't be checked), failed (found, and the check failed), missing (looked for, none), unknown (couldn't be looked for), or not-applicable (e.g. a rebase record for an image never rebased).

timestamp.description: Timestamp is when it was signed or produced (RFC 3339), if known.

Factory.description: Factory describes an image built or rebased by clearcutt-factory, from its verified recipe or rebase record.

inputs.description: Inputs counts what the lock pins.

kind.description: Kind is Image or App. A rebased image's comes from the recipe of the image it was rebased from; it is absent when that couldn't be read.

name.description: Name is the manifest's metadata.name (absent like kind).

rebasedFrom.description: RebasedFrom is the image whose layers were rebased (repository@digest).

sourceDateEpoch.description: SourceDateEpoch is the build timestamp all files were clamped to.

stack.description: Stack is the stack an app was built on.

version.description: Version is the clearcutt-factory version that built or rebased it.

FactoryInputs.description: FactoryInputs counts a factory lock's pins.

Finding.description: Finding is one vulnerability in one package version.

fixedIn.description: FixedIn lists versions with a fix; empty when none is known.

platforms.description: Platforms are the platform images it was found in.

suppressed.description: Suppressed says a VEX statement covers it (it is not counted).

Generator.description: Generator is the tool that wrote the report.

Image.description: Image is one image: a repository at the digest its tags point at.

base.description: Base is the image this one is built on; absent for roots and for images whose base couldn't be determined.

created.description: Created is the image's creation time from its config (RFC 3339), if set.

digest.description: Digest is what the tags point at: a multi-platform index or a single image manifest.

factory.description: Factory is present for images built or rebased by clearcutt-factory.

id.description: ID is unique within the report and stable across runs for the same repository, e.g. ghcr-io-acme-images-billing.

packages.description: Packages is how many package versions the image ships, when known.

repository.description: Repository is registry/path without tag or digest.

root.description: Root says why the image has no parent, when it is a root.

source.description: Source is the code the image was built from, when it says.

unresolved.description: Unresolved gives the reasons no base was found, when it wasn't.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerabilities is absent when the image has no vulnerability data; that means unknown, not clean.

Metadata.description: Metadata identifies the estate and the run.

generatedAt.description: GeneratedAt is when the run finished (RFC 3339).

name.description: Name identifies the estate, e.g. acme-production.

sources.description: Sources are the registries and repositories that were read.

PackageSummary.description: PackageSummary counts images by whether their package set is known.

PackageUse.description: PackageUse is one package version and the images that ship it.

type.description: Type is the ecosystem: apk, deb, rpm, golang, npm, pypi, maven, nix, …

Platform.description: Platform is one platform image of a multi-platform image.

size.description: Size is the total compressed size of the layers, in bytes.

Policy.description: Policy is what images were held to.

failOn.description: FailOn fails images with vulnerabilities at or above this severity (negligible, low, medium, high, critical); empty never fails.

maxDaysBehind.description: MaxDaysBehind fails images whose base is more than this many days behind its newest version; 0 never fails.

maxScanAgeDays.description: MaxScanAgeDays leaves images unverified whose vulnerability scan is older than this many days at the time of the report (what was found since is unknown); 0 accepts any age.

onlyFixed.description: OnlyFixed counts only vulnerabilities that have a fix toward FailOn.

reproduce.description: Reproduce reports whether this run rebuilt images to check them.

required.description: Required lists the evidence kinds an image needs, verified, to pass: any of signature, sbom, vulnerabilityScan, provenance, recipe, tests.

trustedSigners.description: TrustedSigners are the identities whose signatures and attestations count as verified. Empty means nothing can be verified, only present.

Reproducibility.description: Reproducibility is whether rebuilding the image gives the same digest.

checkedAt.description: CheckedAt is when it was checked (RFC 3339).

digest.description: Digest is what the rebuild produced.

method.description: Method is recipe-rebuild (rebuilt from the signed recipe) or rebase-repeat (repeated the recorded rebase).

status.description: Status is reproduced, not-reproduced (the rebuild gave a different digest), not-checked (a recipe exists but this run didn't rebuild, or the rebuild couldn't finish; see detail), or no-recipe (nothing to rebuild from).

Signer.description: Signer is a signing identity: a keyless certificate identity (exact or as a regular expression) with its OIDC issuer, or a public key. In the policy it is who is trusted; on evidence, who signed it, as the certificate says. The source fields matter for reusable GitHub workflows. Their certificate identity is the called workflow, which any repository can call, so a trusted signer for one should say which calling repositories it accepts.

key.description: Key names a public key (a file name or KMS URI), never key material.

sourceMatchesImage.description: SourceMatchesImage, in the policy, requires the run to be in the repository the image names as its source (org.opencontainers.image.source).

sourceRef.description: SourceRef is the ref the run was on, e.g. refs/heads/main. In the policy, signatures must come from runs on it.

sourceRepository.description: SourceRepository is the repository whose workflow run signed, e.g. https://github.com/acme/billing (the certificate's Source Repository URI). In the policy, signatures must come from runs in it.

sourceRepositoryOwner.description: SourceRepositoryOwner, in the policy, accepts runs in any of the owner's repositories, e.g. https://github.com/acme.

Source.description: Source is a registry namespace that was read.

namespace.description: Namespace is a repository path prefix, e.g. acme/images.

registry.description: Registry is a host, e.g. ghcr.io.

repositories.description: Repositories are the repositories read, when they were named rather than enumerated.

SourceRef.description: SourceRef is the code an image was built from.

basis.description: Basis is where this came from: provenance (verified), label, or annotation.

revision.description: Revision is a commit or tag, when known.

StatusCounts.description: StatusCounts counts images by evidence status.

Summary.description: Summary holds the estate's headline numbers.

evidence.description: Evidence counts images by status for each evidence kind (keys: signature, sbom, vulnerabilityScan, provenance, recipe, rebase, tests).

images.description: Images is the number of images in the report.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerabilities totals findings over scanned images.

Verdict.description: Verdict is whether the image meets the policy.

reasons.description: Reasons explain a failed or unverified verdict, one requirement each.

status.description: Status is verified (meets every requirement), failed (violates one), or unverified (some requirement couldn't be decided).

Vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerabilities is an image's vulnerability findings.

scannedAt.description: ScannedAt is when the scan ran (RFC 3339); findings describe that day.

scanner.description: Scanner is the scanner and version, e.g. grype 0.118.0.

source.description: Source is attestation (the publisher's signed report) or scan (this run scanned the image or its SBOM).

VulnerabilitySummary.description: VulnerabilitySummary totals findings over the images that were scanned.

fixable.description: Fixable counts the findings that have a fix.

scanned.description: Scanned is how many images have vulnerability data; NotScanned how many don't (their vulnerabilities are unknown, not zero).

description: Report is one verification run over an image estate.

bases.description: Bases are the base-image repositories that images were found to be built on, with their newest observed version.

images.description: Images are the observed images, one per repository and digest.

packages.description: Packages index which images ship which package versions. Only images whose package set could be read appear here; the rest are counted in summary.packages.unknown, so a package's absence is not proof that no image ships it.

policy.description: Policy is what images were held to in this run.

warnings.description: Warnings are estate-wide problems the run hit.

title: ClearCutt estate report
